findings: The client retained an unsubmitted profile change after an avatar import exhausted its retry budget, while the server already held the ready copy.
The account home header always rendered V2AvatarPlaceholder, even when an avatar had been saved.
changes: Query the account-bound original avatar import locator before attempting idempotent creation.
Resume an uncertain import with the same operation and target media identity instead of creating a second copy.
Keep expired or rejected imports on the existing replacement path.
Refresh the pending source references and distinguish incomplete avatar preparation from active progress.
Render the confirmed account avatar through the authorized presentation pipeline and refresh the view when its media identity changes.

path: Register two independently scoped test accounts through the real UI
Select a synthetic blue image from the system photo picker and send it as a real message
Choose that indexed image as the owner's avatar and save
Require the server-committed feedback and verify the actual image pixels in the profile editor
Verify actual avatar image pixels on the account home page
Relaunch the application, restore the same test account and verify the avatar pixels again
Clean up both local test credential and storage scopes

limits: The original app did not persist the initial import error classification; its exact first-response failure is not established.
The live end-to-end scenario covers selection from existing images. It does not exercise file-picker avatar upload or every image format.
The physical phone was locked after the final installation, so automatic launch was denied. Actual avatar pixels were verified on the live-account simulator.
